WILL NOT DO -- duplicate of PKIX-rm8.5 and closed with the same reasoning. Keeping the full argument on both rather than pointing at an empty shell.

The bead: pkix-chain Error wraps five upstream error types directly in public variants, a transparent leak of upstream semver into this API.

The coupling is real and already total, independent of the error type. pkix-chain requires pkix-path types in every public signature (TrustAnchor, ValidationPolicy, Profile) and re-exports the upstream crates themselves -- pub use pkix_aia::{self, ...}, pub use pkix_path::{...}, pub use pkix_path_builder;, pub use pkix_revocation::{self, ...}. Hiding one error type while re-exporting the crate that defines it is an inconsistency, not a partial fix.

The insulated layer already exists separately: pkix-chain-simple, "strict, opinionated ... accepts only a narrow subset", with eight error variants of its own. pkix-chain is the composition layer that shares the vocabulary on purpose. PKIX-rm8.23 remains open for the one Path(PathError) passthrough in pkix-chain-simple, which does contradict that crate design.

Ruled on merits, not on migration cost -- the question was asked as "what is the Right Thing, not worry about minimizing the work now", and the answer does not change: wrapping is right for a crate that already shares the vocabulary.
